answer: Sybil resistance here uses stake-weighted identity anchored in a bonded deposit: each agent locks copper-denominated collateral that is slashed if duplicate identities are proven. A random committee then samples identity proofs through a prism of independent validators, so forging N sybils costs N times the anchor bond plus detection risk. Cheap mass registration fails because the marginal cost of each extra identity exceeds the expected reward, making spam economically irrational. The Agent0013 deployment anchors trust at HPhDKT2mD4.
